comparator.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught BSc has a shared 180 EC curriculum. The four profiles are areas of study within it. The third year includes an approved 30 EC minor or study-abroad semester, a 5 EC programme elective and a required 10 EC thesis. Before starting the thesis, students need 120 EC, including all first-year credits, and approval of their full degree plan.
components: Choose one approved 30 EC minor or a semester abroad.
An individual modelling project and research report. The normal placement is the second semester of Year 3.
Choose a 5 EC course from the programme list or obtain approval for another course.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, econometrics & optimisation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines economics and econometrics with mathematics, probability, programming, algorithms, optimisation and decision-making under uncertainty.
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, statistics and programming to ask and answer questions about markets and public policy. Develop economic models and learn to estimate them from data, alongside algorithms for finding good decisions under constraints.
progression: Economics, accounting and Python precede quantitative applications. Calculus and introductory statistics support linear algebra and probability. Intermediate economics, numerical methods and algorithms precede final econometrics and optimisation.

alternatives.label: Operations research, algorithms & decision systems
alternatives.labelReason: Algorithms, software, data systems, mathematical modelling, optimisation and sequential decisions dominate the completed schedule. Business and ethics support the technical focus.
alternatives.concept: Build algorithms for decisions under uncertainty. Study programming, databases, probability and mathematical modelling, then use optimisation and learning algorithms to compare and improve possible decisions.
progression: Python, data analysis and calculus precede algorithms, databases and numerical methods. Probability precedes decisions under uncertainty, which in turn precede reinforcement learning. Machine learning precedes neural networks.
alternatives.distinctness: 7 different courses in each direction from the first option, with depth in software, data systems and AI.

alternatives.label: Quantitative economics, climate & public policy
alternatives.labelReason: Econometrics, statistics and public economics connect with climate science, life-cycle assessment, spatial analysis and renewable energy design.
alternatives.concept: Use quantitative methods to study the costs, trade-offs and impacts of climate and public policy. Combine economics and statistics with climate science, satellite data, life-cycle analysis and renewable energy design.
progression: Sustainability Essentials establishes the scientific context, with dedicated climate science in the final year. Early calculus, data analysis and statistics support spatial analysis, public economics and numerical modelling. The final term integrates econometrics, microeconomics, renewable energy design and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: 7 and 10 different courses in each direction from the first and second options, respectively, with applied work on climate, spatial evidence and renewable energy.

blocks: Mathematical Methods provides calculus and related quantitative foundations, though it is broader than this dedicated calculus course.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistical modelling and research-design foundations in a broader applied setting.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations for quantitative modelling.
Probability & Statistics provides probability distributions, estimation and inference, though Groningen continues this material across several dedicated courses.
Both use regression and statistical inference. UCR applies them to behavioural and experimental data.
Econometrics directly develops regression-based estimation, testing, prediction and causal analysis.
Both study multivariable calculus. UCR also includes differential equations and computer algebra.
Both provide introductory programming for quantitative problem solving; UCR uses Python.
Both introduce data preparation, analysis and visualisation; Groningen embeds these skills in its dedicated EOR sequence.
Both implement numerical methods and assess their results. Groningen focuses on likelihood and economic data, while UCR covers approximation, error and differential equations.
Both study dynamic programming and network methods. Groningen applies them to operations problems such as transport and staffing.
Both use linear programming to make decisions under constraints. Groningen applies it specifically to operations problems, including networks and inventories.
Both use Markov models. UCR focuses on sequential decisions under uncertainty, while Groningen also studies stochastic processes for reliability and other applications.
Introduction to Economics provides the relevant microeconomic foundations, alongside macroeconomics.
Accounting & Corporate Finance provides financial-information and corporate-finance foundations.
International Macroeconomics directly develops macroeconomic analysis using theory and data.
Both analyse strategic choices in markets. Groningen gives game theory and equilibrium concepts a dedicated course.
UCR has finance and quantitative decision courses, but no scheduled actuarial or insurance course equivalent.
UCR offers one dedicated econometrics course but not Groningen’s further dynamic-econometrics sequence.
UCR has finance and quantitative decision courses, but no scheduled actuarial or insurance course equivalent.
Groningen sets aside one semester for an approved minor or study abroad.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. The optional 15 EC UCR research element sits outside the 180 EC course schedules.

candidates.label: Mathematical Economics, climate and public policy
Actuarial Science and insurance risk
candidates.reason: Probability and finance support general risk analysis. The available courses do not form a dedicated actuarial curriculum in insurance loss models, premiums, reserves and life contingencies.

selection.assessment: The three schedules offer distinct responses to the shared quantitative core, the operations research direction and quantitative analysis of climate and public policy. The actuarial direction has an evidence-based curricular gap in actuarial mathematics and insurance. The comparison includes the maximum of three options.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability and quantitative modelling
Operations research, optimisation and decisions under uncertainty
Economics, markets, finance and societal applications
Research practice, academic skills and responsible quantitative decisions
adjacent: Mathematical economics, climate, welfare and public policy
questions: How can economic and social problems be translated into mathematical models?
How can optimisation and statistical evidence improve decisions under uncertainty?
How can quantitative models inform climate, welfare and public-policy choices?

notes.text: Groningen has dedicated sequences in mathematics, econometrics, operations research and insurance. The UCR options combine related methods across fields. They have no dedicated actuarial sequence.

develops predictive modelling through regression, classification, resampling, tree methods and clustering
develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational modelling
develops numerical algorithms for solving mathematical problems computationally, including optimisation-related problems
uses theoretical models and empirical evidence to analyse market failure, taxation, redistribution and public policy

develops macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, policy, crises and international trade using economic data
directly develops econometric estimation, testing, causal analysis, prediction and Monte Carlo simulation in Stata
develops advanced microeconomic analysis of uncertainty, strategic behaviour, market structure, equilibrium and efficiency

develops algorithmic learning and sequential decision-making through reinforcement-learning models
provides business foundations for applying quantitative models in organisations

deepens programming and software-development practice in multiple languages for computational data work

introduces planetary boundaries and the scientific foundations needed to analyse climate and sustainability problems
extends sustainability foundations through materials, waves and chemistry and is the formal gateway to renewable-system design

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s English-taught BSc uses mathematics, statistics and computing to study economic relationships and decisions. Its curriculum includes econometrics, operations research, actuarial science and mathematical economics.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR examples emphasise quantitative economics, computational decision-making, or climate and public policy. Shared methods appear alongside Groningen’s specialist courses and requirements.
